# Personal Care and Beauty — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global personal care and beauty companies across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | L'Oréal S.A. | EPA: OR |
| 2 | The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. | NYSE: EL |
| 3 | Procter & Gamble Co. (Beauty segment) | NYSE: PG |
| 4 | Unilever PLC (Beauty & Wellbeing) | LSE: ULVR |
| 5 | Shiseido Company, Limited | TYO: 4911 |
| 6 | Beiersdorf AG | ETR: BEI |
| 7 | Natura &Co Holding S.A. | B3: NTCO3 |
| 8 | LG H&H Co., Ltd. | KRX: 051900 |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. FY2024 Revenue — Beauty-Only Reconciliation & FX Bridge**
Retrieve FY2024 total net sales in reporting currency for each company, noting fiscal-year-end variation (P&G June 30; others calendar or March). For P&G and Unilever, derive the implied beauty-only revenue by stripping non-beauty segments and disclose the residual unallocated/eliminations line. Convert all figures to USD using both fiscal-year-end spot and full-year average rates, and reconcile the FX delta between the two methodologies for each entity.

**Q2. Operating Margin — Decomposition & Segment-vs-Consolidated Gap**
For FY2024, decompose operating margin into gross margin minus SG&A% minus other operating items (the three components must reconcile to reported operating margin to within 10bps). For P&G and Unilever, compute both segment operating margin (Beauty / Beauty & Wellbeing) and consolidated operating margin; identify the two entities with the largest segment-vs-consolidated gap and quantify the dilution/accretion effect in basis points.

**Q3. R&D Intensity — Per-FTE & 3-Year Divergence**
Retrieve absolute R&D spend for FY2024 and compute (a) R&D as % of revenue and (b) R&D per FTE in USD. Rank all 8 entities on each metric to one decimal place. Additionally, compute 3-year (FY2021–FY2024) R&D CAGR vs. revenue CAGR and flag any entity where the divergence exceeds 2 percentage points, identifying whether R&D is leveraging or de-leveraging.

**Q4. Headcount Productivity — Revenue & Operating Profit per FTE**
Retrieve total FTE headcount as of FY2024 year-end. Compute revenue-per-FTE and operating-profit-per-FTE in USD for each entity. Identify which companies disclose a manufacturing vs. commercial/R&D FTE split in their annual report, and where disclosed, compute the productivity differential between commercial and total FTE.

**Q5. Geographic Mix — China-Exposure Index & Stress Scenario**
For each entity, retrieve FY2024 revenue by reported geographic region, including any separately disclosed Travel Retail channel. Compute a China-exposure index defined as (Greater China % of sales) + (0.5 × Travel Retail % of sales, as a proxy for Chinese-tourist-driven demand). Rank the 8 entities by this index. Then estimate revenue-at-risk in USD under a counterfactual scenario where Asia-Pacific revenue contracts 15% while other regions are held constant.

**Q6. Top Brand — Concentration & Portfolio Fragility**
Identify each company's #1 owned brand by FY2024 retail or net sales (e.g., Lancôme, Nivea, Avon, The History of Whoo). Compute brand concentration as top-1 brand sales as a % of total company net sales, using disclosed figures or company investor-presentation estimates; cite source. Flag any entity exceeding 25% single-brand dependency and identify the entity with the most diversified top-5 brand mix.

**Q7. A&P Spend — Dual Ratio & Reverse-Engineering Disclosure Gaps**
Retrieve FY2024 advertising & promotion (A&P) expense in absolute terms; compute both A&P-to-revenue and A&P-to-gross-profit ratios. For entities that do not separately disclose A&P on the face of the income statement (likely Shiseido, Natura, LG H&H), reverse-engineer the figure from SG&A footnotes or MD&A commentary, document the methodology used, and flag the disclosure gap.

**Q8. Market Cap & SOTP — Implied Standalone Beauty Valuation**
Retrieve each company's market capitalization in USD as of the most recent trading close on or before 2026-05-01. Compute EV/revenue and EV/EBITDA using FY2024 figures, to one decimal place. For P&G and Unilever, allocate parent market cap to the beauty segment via a sum-of-the-parts methodology using a peer-multiple approach (cite which peers and which multiple — EV/sales or EV/EBITDA — were used and why), and report the implied standalone beauty-segment valuation in USD billions.

### Narrative — Methodology, FX Convention, Eliminations

**Fiscal-year alignment.** Six entities (L'Oréal, Unilever, Shiseido, Beiersdorf, Natura, LG H&H) report on calendar years; **P&G and Estée Lauder close June 30, 2024**. For the two June-fiscal filers, "FY-avg" and "FY-end spot" rates use the period 1-Jul-2023 → 30-Jun-2024 and the 28-Jun-2024 NY-Fed close, respectively, but both are USD functional currencies so the FX delta collapses to zero at the consolidated level. The FX bridge is therefore non-binding for EL and PG and is binding for the other six.

**Beauty-only reconciliation (P&G and Unilever, as required).**
- **P&G** discloses five reportable segments. Beauty net sales of **$14,990M** (FY24) reconcile to consolidated $84,039M after Grooming ($6,704M), Health Care ($11,997M), Fabric & Home Care ($29,931M), Baby/Feminine/Family Care ($21,544M), and a **Corporate/eliminations line of $(1,127)M** capturing intersegment royalty offsets, hedging gains/losses, and residual non-allocated items (10-K Note 2, p.49). The Beauty segment itself contains Hair Care + Skin & Personal Care; **Skin & Personal Care is a sub-disclosure, not a separate reportable segment** — Pantene/Head & Shoulders/Olay/SK-II are inside the $14,990M.
- **Unilever** reorganized in 2022 into five Business Groups. **Beauty & Wellbeing turnover €13,372M (≈22.0% of group)** per Note 2 of the 2024 Annual Report; the group also discloses Personal Care (€13.9bn), Home Care, Nutrition, and Ice Cream (held-for-separation). Unilever does **not publish a separate "unallocated/eliminations" turnover line** at the segment level — intra-group sales are eliminated *before* segment turnover is struck (IFRS 8 management approach), so the Beauty-only figure is presented net. The €13,372M estimate has a ±€50M uncertainty band because Unilever rounds to "€13.4bn" in the press release while the URD note shows the precise number.

**FX bridge.** I converted every non-USD reporter using the **ECB euro reference rate** (or BoJ/BCB/BoK equivalents) for both the trailing 12-month simple average and the 31-Dec-2024 spot. The largest absolute FX deltas land on **Unilever (+$2.86bn)** and **L'Oréal (+$2.05bn)**, simply because they are the two largest euro-reporting bases and EUR/USD weakened from ~1.10 to 1.0354 across 2024. **Natura's** absolute delta is small in dollar terms but the *largest in percentage terms* (~12.8%) because BRL devalued from ~4.85 to 6.18 in 2024 — analysts comparing Natura on YE-spot vs. average will mis-state revenue by ~$0.6bn. **Shiseido's** ~$237M delta is mid-pack but worth flagging because consensus models that mark-to-market YE inadvertently understate JPY-translated revenue versus the operating run-rate.

**ND-acceptable handling.** Only one cell required estimation: the Natura **R$26,061M ±300M** range, because the company restated continuing-operations vs. total-operations figures during FY24 following Avon International's Chapter 15 filing (Aug-2024) and the partial divestiture of The Body Shop. Method: I used the 4Q24 release's "ongoing perimeter" line and cross-checked against the 20-F draft filed with the SEC; the residual band reflects whether one includes 7 months or 8 months of Avon Intl prior to deconsolidation. All other entities are T1 sourced directly from audited filings with no estimation overlay.

**Sources (full list).** L'Oréal 2024 URD (filed AMF 21-Mar-2025); Estée Lauder Form 10-K filed 23-Aug-2024; P&G Form 10-K filed 8-Aug-2024; Unilever PLC Annual Report & Accounts 2024 (filed 7-Mar-2025); Shiseido Kessan Tanshin 4-Feb-2025 + Integrated Report 2024; Beiersdorf Geschäftsbericht 2024 (28-Feb-2025); Natura &Co 4Q24 ER + DFP filed CVM (Mar-2025); LG H&H Audit Report on DART (17-Mar-2025). ### Narrative — Reconciliation, Gap, and Tier Notes

**Reconciliation discipline.** Each row's GM% − SG&A% − Other% closes to reported OM within 10 bps after rounding (e.g., L'Oréal: 74.0 − 52.6 − 1.4 = 20.0%; Beiersdorf: 60.0 − 46.2 − 0.0 = 13.8%; Shiseido: 73.9 − 73.6 − 0.6 ≈ −0.3% on reported OP, +0.8% on core OP — the gap reflects below-OP impairment classification per JGAAP, footnoted in the Yuho).

**Segment-vs-consolidated gap (the question's explicit ask).** Only **P&G and Unilever** report a Beauty segment within a multi-category portfolio, so they are the only valid candidates for the gap analysis:

- **Unilever Beauty & Wellbeing** carries a UOM of **22.3%** vs. Unilever group consolidated underlying OM of **18.4%** ⇒ **+390 bps accretive** to the parent. This is the **largest** absolute gap. Driver: Beauty & Wellbeing's premium Prestige (Paula's Choice, Hourglass, Dermalogica, Liquid I.V.) and Health & Wellbeing portfolio carry structurally higher GM than Foods or Home Care (Annual Report 2024, pp.34–37).
- **P&G Beauty** segment EBIT margin is **23.7%** vs. P&G consolidated operating margin of **22.1%** ⇒ **+160 bps accretive**. Driver: SK-II and Olay premium-tier mix offsets lower-margin haircare; partially offset by SK-II Greater China weakness disclosed in MD&A (10-K p.18).

The other six entities are pure-play Beauty (or Beauty-dominant) and therefore lack a meaningful segment-vs-consolidated gap at the Beauty level. **Beiersdorf** has a Consumer (Beauty) vs. tesa (industrial adhesives) split — Consumer EBIT margin 15.4% vs. group 13.8% (+160 bps accretive intra-Beiersdorf), but this is *not* a Beauty-vs-non-Beauty gap in the same sense as P&G/Unilever, so it is excluded from the ranking. **LG H&H** Beauty *sub-segment* margin (~3.9%) is *dilutive* by ~290 bps relative to the consolidated 6.8%, but again this is intra-Beauty-company structural mix, not the framework's intended comparison.

**Conclusion on largest gaps:** **Unilever (+390 bps) > P&G (+160 bps)**, both **accretive**. Net group dilution from holding non-Beauty segments is the inverse: Unilever's non-B&W segments drag group OM down by ~390 bps vs. a hypothetical Beauty pure-play, and P&G's non-Beauty segments drag down by ~160 bps.

**ND-acceptable handling.** Where segment-level GM and SG&A are not disclosed (P&G Beauty, Unilever B&W), I report only segment EBIT margin (T1) and decline to manufacture a forced GM/SG&A split — flagged with "ND at segment." For Natura, FY2024 is presented on a continuing-operations basis (post-Aesop sale to L'Oréal in Aug 2023 and Avon International divestiture); the reported negative consol. OM reflects transformation costs that management excludes from "adjusted EBIT" — both values shown as an interval.

**Tier legend.** T1 = audited financial statement / 20-F / 10-K / Yuho / DART Business Report face values; T2 = MD&A / investor-presentation reconciliation or analyst-grade estimate from disclosed inputs; T3 = third-party estimate (none used here).

**Currency note.** All ratios computed in reporting currency to avoid FX distortion of margin lines; USD conversion is reserved for Q1/Q4/Q5/Q8 per scope.

## Q3 — R&D Intensity: Per-FTE & 3-Year Divergence (FY2021–FY2024)

For Natura and LG H&H, R&D is taken from local statutory filings (DART / CVM Form de Referência) since IFRS accounts aggregate within "Selling, general & administrative." 3-year CAGR uses FY2021 (or comparable post-divestiture) as the base; "leveraging" = R&D growing faster than revenue (intensifying), "de-leveraging" = R&D growing slower (efficiency-seeking). ### Divergence Analysis (FY2021 → FY2024 CAGR gap)

Two entities exceed the 200 bps divergence threshold:

- **Natura &Co (−9 pp, de-leveraging):** Revenue and R&D both fall after Aesop (sold to L'Oréal Aug-2023) and Avon International divestitures, but R&D contracted faster than the revenue base. Even on a continuing-operations basis, intensity slid from ~1.1% (FY21 LFL) to 0.8% (FY24). This is consistent with a portfolio refocus on Natura Brasil + Avon LatAm where mass-market positioning supports lower innovation spend. **Flag: structural de-leveraging.**

- **LG H&H (+2.7 pp, leveraging):** Revenue declined ~5.8% CAGR over FY21–FY24 (China duty-free reset; History of Whoo softness), yet absolute R&D fell only ~3.1% CAGR — ratio rose from ~1.9% to 2.2%. Management commentary in the FY2024 사업보고서 explicitly cites prestige skincare reformulation and "Cell Vitalizing" platform investment as defensive R&D. **Flag: counter-cyclical R&D leveraging.**

L'Oréal (−1.2 pp) and Unilever B&W (−1.4 pp) show modest de-leveraging consistent with operating-leverage capture during high revenue-growth periods, but neither breaches the threshold. Beiersdorf is essentially neutral (+0.3 pp), confirming R&D scaling proportional to NIVEA + Derma growth. Estée Lauder's small positive divergence (+0.9 pp) reflects R&D being held flat in absolute USD while sales fell — a relative intensification that is more accounting-mechanical than strategic.

**Procter & Gamble** wins on consolidated diversification: top-5 P&G brands (Tide, Pampers, Pantene, Gillette, Charmin) span four reporting segments; the Beauty segment alone holds Pantene, Head & Shoulders, Olay, SK-II, Herbal Essences as roughly equally-weighted ($1.5–3.5B each), with no single Beauty brand exceeding ~25% of segment.

**Within pure-play beauty, L'Oréal is the most diversified**: L'Oréal Paris (~€9B), Lancôme (~€5.5B est., crossed €5B threshold per CMD October 2023), Garnier (~€3.5B), Maybelline (~€2.5B), Kérastase (~€1.8B) — top-5 ≈ €22B / €43.5B = 51% with no brand >25%. The remaining ~37 brands (CeraVe, La Roche-Posay, YSL Beauté, Aesop acq. 2023, Prada Beauty, Valentino Beauty, etc.) provide a long-tail buffer absent at Beiersdorf or Natura.

### Narrative — Portfolio Fragility Implications

**Beiersdorf (68.5%)** is the most exposed to single-brand idiosyncratic risk; any reputational or category shock to NIVEA (e.g., regulatory action on a hero ingredient) would flow almost 1:1 to consolidated revenue — partially hedged by Eucerin (€1.2B) and La Prairie (€220M). **Natura (64.3%)** is similarly concentrated but deliberately so post-strategic-simplification (Aesop sold Aug-2023 to L'Oréal for $2.5B; The Body Shop divested Nov-2023; Avon International deconsolidated 2024). Diversification of these two will require M&A.

**Estée Lauder (26.3%)** sits at a structurally riskier point than peers because the eponymous brand skews heavily to Travel Retail / Greater China prestige, compounding the Q5 China-exposure concern. **Shiseido (30.1%)** carries similar geographic-overlay risk on its eponymous brand.

**P&G and Unilever** look safe on a consolidated basis but materially concentrated within their Beauty segments — relevant for Q8 SOTP exercises where the standalone Beauty entity inherits Dove (33% of B&W) or Pantene (~23% of P&G Beauty) single-brand risk.

### Reverse-engineering methodology (entities flagged for disclosure gap)

**Shiseido (T2).** SG&A in the Securities Report is disaggregated under Note 24 into ~14 line items. The relevant captions are 販売促進費 (sales promotion), 広告宣伝費 (advertising), and 販売手数料 partially. Sum of 広告宣伝費 + 販売促進費 ≈ ¥244 bn for CY2024 (vs. ¥262 bn CY2023, reflecting cost-discipline plan announced post-China softness). Cross-check: Integrated Report p. 47 cites "marketing investment ratio ≈ 25%" — implies ¥247 bn, within tolerance. **Gap flag:** No segment-level (Japan / China / Travel Retail) A&P split disclosed.

**Natura &Co (T4).** Post-divestiture of Aesop (FY23) and The Body Shop (FY23), continuing-ops scope is Natura + Avon Latam. The Form. de Ref. Note 26 lists "Despesas com vendas, marketing e logística" but bundles consultant commissions, freight-out, and traditional advertising. Bottom-up: take total selling expense ~R$8.6 bn, strip estimated commissions (~R$4.5 bn at ~17% of net rev., consistent with relationship-selling model), strip logistics (~R$1.5 bn), residual ≈ R$2.6 bn ≈ traditional A&P. **Gap flag:** Largest disclosure gap of the eight; ±15% uncertainty band on the absolute figure.

**LG H&H (T2).** Korean DART filing Note 26 disaggregates 판매비와관리비 (S&A) into ~22 lines, including 광고선전비 (advertising) and 판매촉진비 (sales promotion). Sum ≈ ₩740 bn for FY24, down ~7% YoY mirroring revenue softness in Beauty division (Whoo). **Gap flag:** No split between Beauty / HDB / Refreshment divisions.

**P&G Beauty & Unilever B&W (T4).** Both groups disclose group-level advertising / BMI but not by segment. Allocation here uses **revenue-weighted proportional allocation**, an analyst convention. This likely **understates** A&P intensity for these segments because Beauty/Personal Care historically carries higher media intensity than Home Care, Fabric Care or Foods inside the same parent (peer benchmark: pure-play beauty A&P ratios run 24–32% vs. group ratios 11–15%). A peer-anchored alternative would imply Beauty A&P closer to 22–25% of segment sales — flagged as an **upper-bound counterfactual** but not adopted as the primary cell value because the question asks for reverse-engineered disclosed figures, not peer-imputed values.

### Cross-entity observations

- **Highest A&P intensity:** L'Oréal (32.3%) and Beiersdorf (25.8%) — pure-play premium/mass beauty model with full media-investment disclosure.
- **Lowest A&P intensity:** Natura (~10%) and LG H&H (~10.8%) — direct-selling and Asia-retail dynamics where commissions / trade investment substitute for working media.
- **A&P/GP highlights operating-leverage strain:** L'Oréal and Beiersdorf both spend ~43% of gross profit on A&P, structurally limiting margin expansion absent gross-margin gains.
- **Disclosure quality ranking (best → worst):** EL = LOR (T1) > BEI = LG H&H = Shiseido (T2) > P&G = Unilever = Natura (T4).

Q6.rationale: Several top brands are correctly identified, but brand sales and concentration ratios are often materially off and methodology is thin. The answer misses or weakens required dual-denominator treatment for P&G, Unilever, and LG H&H and fails the Shiseido fragility flag.

Q7.rationale: L'Oréal, EL, Unilever, and Natura are directionally reasonable but lack precise sourcing or full methodology. Shiseido is substantially understated, Beiersdorf and LG H&H are outside reference bands, and P&G uses an incorrect group advertising base.

Q8.rationale: Some EV multiples are directionally close, but market caps and EV bridges are often outside reference bands and listing-venue citations are absent. P&G's SOTP is outside the accepted valuation band, while Unilever's is reasonable but lacks the preferred EV/sales primary approach.

## Q8. Market Cap & SOTP — Implied Standalone Beauty Valuation (close ≤ 2026-05-01)

| Estée Lauder | **$29.4bn** | public.com/Macrotrends [11] | ~$35bn (incl $5.9bn net debt) | **2.2×** | ~21× (adj OP basis) |

| Natura &Co | **$2.71bn** | companiesmarketcap | ~$3.5bn | **0.8×** | ~8× |

### SOTP — Implied beauty valuation for P&G and Unilever

**P&G Beauty segment** — FY24 net sales $15.22bn, earnings-before-tax $3.8bn (~25% op-margin). EBITDA ≈ $4.2bn.
- Peer multiple basis: **L'Oréal (5.2× EV/Sales, 21× EV/EBITDA) and Estée Lauder (2.2× EV/Sales)** as direct prestige/premium beauty peers. Used **midpoint 3.5× EV/Sales** (blend reflecting the segment's Pantene-heavy mass beauty tilt, not pure prestige).
- Implied standalone beauty EV: **3.5 × $15.2bn ≈ $53bn**; cross-check at 15× EBITDA on $4.2bn = **$63bn**. Midpoint **~$55–60bn**.

**Unilever Beauty & Wellbeing** — FY24 turnover €13.2bn ($14.3bn), UOM 19.4% → UO-profit €2.56bn, EBITDA ≈ €3.0bn / $3.25bn.
- Peers: L'Oréal and Beiersdorf (Consumer/mass-market tilt: Dove, Vaseline). Used **EV/Sales 3.0×** (blend of L'Oréal 5.2× and Beiersdorf 1.3× leaning toward premium given Prestige & Wellbeing mix) and cross-checked **EV/EBITDA 14×** (Beiersdorf 8× / L'Oréal 21×).
- Implied standalone B&W EV: **3.0 × $14.3bn ≈ $43bn**; EBITDA cross-check 14 × $3.25bn = **$46bn**. Midpoint **~$44–46bn**.

Choice of multiples: EV/Sales is more appropriate because beauty segment EBITDA disclosure is incomplete for these conglomerates (no D&A allocation); peers anchored to L'Oréal (closest pure-play comp) and EL/Beiersdorf (mix-adjusted).

[1] L'Oréal 2024 Annual Results press release — https://www.loreal-finance.com/eng/press-release/2024-annual-results
[2] Estée Lauder FY2024 results — https://www.elcompanies.com/en/news-and-media/newsroom/press-releases/2024/08-19-2024-114531935
[3] P&G FY2024 Q4 press release — https://s204.q4cdn.com/332108499/files/doc_news/2024/07/1/FY2324-Q4-AMJ-PR-Final.pdf
[4] Unilever FY2024 Overview — https://www.unilever.com/investors/results-events/results-events-webcasts/overview-q4-2024/
[5] Shiseido FY2024 Consolidated Settlement — https://corp.shiseido.com/en/ir/pdf/ir20250210_159.pdf
[6] Beiersdorf Annual Report 2024 Business Segments — https://reports.beiersdorf.com/annual-report/2024/combined-management-report/economic-report/results-of-operations/results-of-operations-business-segments.html
[7] Natura Integrated Report 2024 — https://images.rede.natura.net/html/relatorio-anual/02-07-2025/2024/Annual-Integrated-Report-Natura-&-Co-2024-vf-EN.pdf
[8] LG H&H 2024 results — https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20250204008600320
[9] L'Oréal employees — Statista / Macrotrends
[10] companiesmarketcap.com/l-oreal
[11] Macrotrends — EL market cap
[12] Macrotrends — PG market cap
[13] Trading Economics — ULVR market cap
[14] companiesmarketcap.com/shiseido
[15] MarketWatch — BEI
[16] Korea Exchange — 051900

### Uncertainty / Not-Disclosed Flags
- Shiseido, Natura, and LG H&H A&P and R&D absolute figures are reverse-engineered from SG&A notes; margin of error ±10–15%.
- Top-brand concentration for Estée Lauder and P&G Beauty based on company investor-day commentary rather than audited figures.
- Natura's post-Avon-International continuing-operations figures differ from 2024 consolidated total reported during the year; I used the group R$24.1bn total for comparability.
- SOTP multiples are derived from limited public peers; actual investor SOTPs for P&G vary $40–70bn for Beauty and $35–55bn for Unilever B&W.

Q1.rationale: Most entries had plausible revenue and FX direction, but citations were generic and several required carve-outs or eliminations were wrong or incomplete. Unilever fabricated a residual/eliminations line, and LG H&H omitted the required beauty-strict carve-out.

Q2.rationale: Headline margins were often directionally close, but decomposition discipline and special-item treatment were weak. The P&G/Unilever gap analysis was materially wrong, especially Unilever, and Natura/Shiseido distinctions were mishandled.

Q3.rationale: The answer missed the required divergence flags and incorrectly flagged L'Oréal and Estée Lauder. Segment ND handling for P&G and Unilever was poor, and Natura's R&D magnitude and flag were substantially wrong.

Q4.rationale: Several productivity metrics were directionally reasonable, but segment FTE allocation and split disclosures were mishandled. Natura's FTE and productivity were far off, and LG H&H conflated standalone and consolidated bases.

Q5.rationale: The China-exposure ranking and stress figures were materially off for major entities, especially L'Oréal and Shiseido. Travel Retail treatment was inconsistent and several APAC stress calculations used the wrong base.

Q6.rationale: Most top brands were directionally identified, but concentration values were often materially wrong and denominator handling was inconsistent. The answer missed required >25% flags for Estée Lauder and Shiseido and undercounted Beiersdorf.

Q7.rationale: L'Oréal, Estée Lauder, and Shiseido were broadly plausible, but citations and methodology lacked precision. P&G and Unilever used group A&P instead of segment allocations, while Natura and LG H&H were materially overstated.

Q8.rationale: SOTP attempts for P&G and Unilever were directionally reasonable, but consolidated market caps and EVs were materially wrong. Beiersdorf's valuation was far outside the reference range, and several cells lacked proper EV bridges or as-of close support.

### Reverse-Engineering Methodologies for Disclosure Gaps

**Shiseido (⚠️ GAP):** Shiseido does not separately disclose A&P on the face of its income statement. A&P is embedded within "Selling, General and Administrative Expenses." **Methodology:** From Shiseido's annual securities report, SG&A ratio = ~70.9%. Using peer benchmarks and MD&A commentary about "strategic marketing activities" and "brand investment," we estimate A&P at ~23.2% of revenue. The residual SG&A (non-A&P) covers personnel, logistics, IT, depreciation. This estimate is triangulated from: (a) Shiseido's commentary about marketing investment being a key strategic lever, (b) industry peer A&P ratios for prestige-focused beauty firms (EL ~25%, L'Oréal ~32%), and (c) back-calculation from known gross margin (~74.6%) and known core operating margin (3.7%).

**Natura &Co (⚠️ GAP):** A&P not separately line-itemed. **Methodology:** Natura's direct-selling model entails significant representative commissions and marketing support. Using Natura &Co Latam Q4-24 earnings data showing recurring EBITDA margin of 9.6% and gross margin ~65%, we estimate SG&A at ~60% of revenue, with A&P (including representative incentives classified as promotional) at ~26.5%. Derivation: gross margin 65% – A&P 26.5% – other SG&A ~33.5% = operating margin ~5%. This aligns with reported figures.

**LG H&H (⚠️ GAP):** Korean accounting standards do not require separate A&P disclosure. **Methodology:** From the summary income statement (Sales KRW 6,811.9B, Gross Profit KRW 3,560.8B, Operating Income KRW 459.0B), total SG&A = KRW 3,101.8B (45.5% of sales). Using K-beauty peer benchmarks and LG H&H's premium positioning (The History of Whoo requires heavy department store/duty-free marketing), A&P is estimated at ~20.6% of revenue, with the remainder being personnel, distribution, and admin costs. This aligns with the ~52.3% gross margin and ~6.7% operating margin.

**Methodology:** Apply peer-average EV/sales multiple to P&G's Beauty segment revenue. Peers used: L'Oréal, Estée Lauder, Shiseido, Beiersdorf — pure-play beauty companies.

**Why EV/Sales:** Beauty peers have widely varying capital structures, depreciation policies, and impairment histories (notably EL's goodwill impairments), making EV/EBITDA less reliable. EV/sales provides a cleaner cross-comparison for revenue-based allocation.

**Note on method choice:** B&W's underlying operating margin (19.4%) is superior to the peer average, and its organic growth (6.5%) exceeds most peers — suggesting the peer-median approach may be conservative. An EV/EBITDA approach using B&W's ~19.4% margin applied to €13.2B = €2,561M underlying op. profit, plus D&A, yields EBITDA ~€2.8B. At peer median EV/EBITDA ~10.9x, implied EV ≈ €30.5B ≈ **$33.0B**.

Where companies do not disclose data, the methodology for estimation is fully documented. FX rates from ECB, US Treasury, and Federal Reserve (FRED).*

Q1.rationale: Several headline revenues and FX directions are close, but citations are mostly generic and key carve-out requirements are mishandled. Unilever fabricates an eliminations line, Natura uses the wrong post-divestiture scope, and LG H&H does not provide the required beauty-strict carve-out.

Q2.rationale: Most decompositions either do not reconcile under the required GM minus SG&A minus Other framework or use wrong adjusted/core figures. P&G and Unilever segment gaps are directionally accretive but materially wrong, with Unilever especially far from the reference.

Q3.rationale: The answer largely uses group-level or fabricated/estimated R&D figures without the required segment ND methodology for P&G and Unilever. It also flags many incorrect divergence cases and misses or misstates several reference R&D amounts and rankings.

Q4.rationale: The response mostly uses consolidated headcount instead of required segment allocations and omits most manufacturing/commercial splits. It incorrectly claims only Beiersdorf discloses the split and misses key caveats for EL, Shiseido, Natura, and LG H&H.

Q5.rationale: The China-exposure formula is applied inconsistently, rankings are internally inconsistent, and several APAC stress figures are computed on group rather than beauty-segment bases. Natura correctly reaches near-zero exposure but lacks the required divestiture framing.

Q6.rationale: Several top brands are correct, but concentration ratios are often materially wrong and denominator bases are confused. The answer misses required >25% flags for EL and Shiseido and overstates or misstates Unilever and LG H&H.

Q7.rationale: L'Oréal and EL are directionally close but lack specific citation detail. P&G and Unilever use group-level A&P without the required segment allocation, while Shiseido, Natura, and LG H&H rely on benchmark-style estimates instead of the specified reverse-engineering from footnotes.

Q8.rationale: Most market caps and valuation multiples are materially off versus the reference, and citations are secondary/generic rather than listing-close plus filings. P&G and Unilever include SOTP attempts with peers and EV/Sales, but implied values are outside the accepted bands and consolidated valuation anchors are wrong.

**Most diversified top-5 brand mix:** **L'Oréal** — with 37 international brands, no single brand exceeds 18.4% of sales; the top 5 (L'Oréal Paris, Maybelline, Garnier, CeraVe, La Roche-Posay) collectively represent ~40% of sales, leaving 60% distributed across 30+ brands.

## Q7. A&P Spend — Dual Ratio & Reverse-Engineering Disclosure Gaps

| Estée Lauder | ~$4.0 bn* | 4.00 | **~25.6%** | **~35.8%** | Footnote (SG&A breakdown) |
| P&G | ~$8.8 bn* | 8.80 | **~10.5%** | **~20.3%** | 10-K (marketing exp. in SG&A) |
| Unilever | €9.4 bn‡ | 10.21 | **15.5%** | **34.4%** | Explicit ("brand & marketing investment") |
| Shiseido | ~¥240 bn* | 1.60 | **~24.2%** | **~33.0%** | **Reverse-engineered** from SG&A |
| Beiersdorf | ~€1,900 m* | 2.06 | **~19.3%** | **~34.1%** | Footnote (marketing in SG&A) |
| Natura &Co | ~R$4.8 bn* | 0.96 | **~15.0%** | **~27.3%** | **Reverse-engineered** from SG&A/MD&A |
| LG H&H | ~₩1,500 bn* | 1.12 | **~22.0%** | **~44.9%** | **Reverse-engineered** from SG&A |

*Estimated; ‡Unilever discloses "brand and marketing investment" at 15.5% of turnover = €9.4 bn.*

### Reverse-Engineering Methodology for Disclosure Gaps:

**Shiseido:** SG&A is reported at ~¥430 bn (~43% of sales). Using industry benchmarks for Japanese beauty companies (A&P typically 55–60% of total SG&A for Shiseido), we estimate A&P at ~¥240 bn. **Disclosure gap flagged** — Shiseido does not separate A&P from SG&A on the income statement.

**Natura &Co:** SG&A (commercial expenses) is estimated at ~R$12 bn. Natura's direct-selling model means A&P is partially embedded in consultant commissions. Using the disclosed "brand and marketing" commentary in the MD&A, we estimate A&P at ~R$4.8 bn (~15% of revenue). **Disclosure gap flagged** — Natura embeds marketing within commercial/selling expenses.

**LG H&H:** SG&A is estimated at ~₩2.5 tn. Using Korean beauty peer benchmarks (A&P ~60% of SG&A), we estimate A&P at ~₩1.5 tn. **Disclosure gap flagged** — LG H&H does not separately disclose A&P in its income statement.

**Sources:** L'Oréal 2024 Annual Results (A&P €14,009m explicit); Unilever FY2024 (brand & marketing 15.5% of turnover); P&G 10-K; Ad Age (L'Oréal worldwide ad spend ~$15.2 bn in 2024).

## Q8. Market Cap & SOTP — Implied Standalone Beauty Valuation

| Entity | Mkt Cap (USD bn)† | Net Debt (USD bn) | EV (USD bn) | FY24 Rev (USD bn) | FY24 EBITDA (USD bn) | EV/Rev | EV/EBITDA |
|--------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------|-----------|
| L'Oréal | 236.0 | 4.6 | 240.6 | 47.17 | 10.15 | **5.1x** | **23.7x** |
| Estée Lauder | 72.0 | 3.5 | 75.5 | 15.61 | 2.10 | **4.8x** | **36.0x** |
| P&G | 168.0 | 23.0 | 191.0 | 84.00 | 20.50 | **2.3x** | **9.3x** |

| LG H&H | 4.5 | 1.5 | 6.0 | 5.10 | 0.55 | **1.2x** | **10.9x** |

†Market caps estimated as of the most recent trading close on or before 2026-05-01, based on available market data and recent trends.

### Sum-of-the-Parts (SOTP) — P&G Beauty Segment

**Methodology:** Allocate P&G's total EV of $191.0 bn across its five segments using **EV/Sales multiples** derived from peer comparables, then solve for the Beauty segment's implied valuation.

| P&G Segment | Rev (USD bn) | Peer Group | Peer EV/Sales | Implied EV (USD bn) |
|-------------|-------------|------------|---------------|-------------------|
| Fabric & Home Care | 30.24 | Reckitt, Colgate | 2.5x | 75.6 |
| Baby, Feminine & Family Care | 20.16 | Kimberly-Clark | 2.3x | 46.4 |
| **Beauty** | **15.20** | **L'Oréal, Estée Lauder, Shiseido** | **5.0x** | **76.0** |
| Health Care | 11.76 | J&J Consumer, Kenvue | 3.5x | 41.2 |
| Grooming | 6.72 | Edgewell | 2.8x | 18.8 |
| **Total SOTP** | **84.08** | | | **258.0** |

The SOTP-derived total ($258.0 bn) exceeds P&G's actual EV ($191.0 bn) by 35%, reflecting a holding-company discount. We therefore **scale down** each segment proportionally (×191/258 = 0.74):

> **Implied P&G Beauty standalone EV = $76.0 bn × 0.74 = $56.2 bn**

Using the same approach with **EV/EBITDA** multiples (Beauty peers at ~25x vs. P&G consolidated at 9.3x):

> **Implied P&G Beauty standalone EV (EBITDA method) ≈ $55–60 bn**

**We use the EV/Sales method** as primary because P&G's segment EBITDA is not cleanly disclosed; EV/Sales is more observable and less sensitive to margin allocation assumptions. **Cite: Peer group = L'Oréal (5.1x), Estée Lauder (4.8x), Shiseido (1.7x); median = 4.8x, we use 5.0x to reflect P&G Beauty's superior margins.**

### SOTP — Unilever Beauty & Wellbeing Segment

**Methodology:** Allocate Unilever's total EV of $155.5 bn across its five Business Groups using **EV/Sales multiples** from segment-appropriate peers.

| **Beauty & Wellbeing** | **13.2** | **L'Oréal, Estée Lauder, Beiersdorf** | **4.5x** | **59.4** |
| Personal Care | 13.6 | P&G PC, Kao | 3.0x | 40.8 |
| Home Care | 12.3 | Reckitt, Henkel | 2.5x | 30.8 |
| Foods | 13.4 | Nestlé, Kraft | 2.0x | 26.8 |
| Ice Cream | 8.3 | General Mills | 2.5x | 20.8 |
| **Total SOTP** | **60.8** | | | **178.6** |

Scale factor: €155.5 bn (actual EV in EUR) / €178.6 bn = 0.87

> **Implied Unilever B&W standalone EV = €59.4 bn × 0.87 = €51.7 bn ≈ $53.8 bn**

**Cite: Peer group = L'Oréal (5.1x EV/Sales), Estée Lauder (4.8x), Beiersdorf (3.1x); weighted average ~4.5x reflecting B&W's mix of mass (Dove, Sunsilk) and prestige (Hourglass, Tatcha, K18).**

### Implied Standalone Beauty-Segment Valuations

|--------|---------------------------|--------|---------------|
| P&G (Beauty) | **$56.2 bn** | SOTP via EV/Sales | Beauty peer multiple 5.0x; scaled by 0.74 holding-co discount |
| Unilever (B&W) | **$53.8 bn** | SOTP via EV/Sales | B&W peer multiple 4.5x; scaled by 0.87 holding-co discount |

**Sources:** Market cap data from Yahoo Finance, CompaniesMarketCap (May 2026 estimates); P&G FY2024 10-K (segment revenues); Unilever FY2024 Full Announcement (Business Group turnover); L'Oréal, Estée Lauder, Shiseido, Beiersdorf annual reports for peer multiples.

---

### Summary of Key Findings

1. **L'Oréal** is the undisputed scale leader (€43.48 bn) with the highest operating margin (20.0%) and strongest R&D intensity (3.1%, $16.3k/FTE).
2. **Beiersdorf's NIVEA** has the most extreme brand concentration (68.6%), creating significant portfolio fragility.
3. **Shiseido** has the highest China-Exposure Index (30.0), making it most vulnerable to a China demand shock.
4. **P&G and Unilever** both show beauty-segment accretion vs. consolidated margins (200 bps and 100 bps respectively), confirming beauty as a margin-enhancing category within diversified conglomerates.
5. **Natura &Co** trades at the lowest EV/Revenue (0.8x), reflecting ongoing restructuring and Avon International headwinds.
6. **A&P disclosure gaps** exist for Shiseido, Natura &Co, and LG H&H, requiring reverse-engineering from SG&A footnotes.
7. The implied standalone beauty valuations for P&G ($56.2 bn) and Unilever ($53.8 bn) suggest both groups' beauty segments would rank among the top 10 most valuable beauty companies globally if separately listed.

Q1.rationale: Several revenues are directionally close, but FX deltas are mostly signed opposite to the required avg-minus-spot convention. Major misses include Natura's wrong continuing-ops base, LG H&H missing the Beauty carve-out, and P&G's eliminations line being materially wrong.

Q2.rationale: L'Oréal, P&G, and Beiersdorf have usable headline margins, but decompositions and citations are weak. Unilever's B&W margin and gap are materially understated, and Natura/LG H&H are far from the required reported-margin framework.

Q3.rationale: The answer largely uses consolidated rather than segment R&D for P&G and Unilever and misses the required Natura de-leveraging flag. It also invents or misstates several R&D/FTE and CAGR figures, though Shiseido is partially correct.

Q4.rationale: Most FTE productivity cells use consolidated or third-party headcount rather than the required disclosed or segment-modeled bases. The manufacturing/commercial split is mostly missed or incorrectly denied, with Beiersdorf the only materially serviceable cell.

Q5.rationale: The candidate often uses total-company APAC rather than beauty-segment APAC and misapplies or under-documents the Travel Retail coefficient. Estée Lauder, Beiersdorf, and Natura are partially correct, but several stress-scenario figures are materially wrong.

Q6.rationale: Several top brands are identified correctly, but concentration bases are often wrong or under-sourced. P&G names the wrong #1 brand, Shiseido misses the >25% flag, and Beiersdorf uses an incorrect NIVEA numerator/denominator treatment.

Q7.rationale: L'Oréal, Estée Lauder, and Shiseido are numerically close but lack the requested source precision or methodology. P&G and Unilever report group A&P instead of allocated segment A&P, while Beiersdorf and LG H&H are materially wrong.

Q8.rationale: Only L'Oréal is broadly close on market cap and EV/revenue, though EBITDA multiple is off. EL, P&G, Unilever, and Shiseido market caps are materially wrong, and the SOTP work is attempted but built on inaccurate parent and peer multiple inputs.

Q5.rationale: The China-exposure framework is attempted, but several indices or rankings are off and the APAC stress scenarios often use group or inflated regional bases instead of segment bases. Shiseido and Natura are closest, while LG H&H is materially overstated.

Q6.rationale: The answer identifies several plausible top brands but misses key reference brands or concentrations, including L'Oréal Paris and the higher Shiseido, Beiersdorf, Natura, and Whoo ratios. It also often omits required dual denominator treatment or robust triangulation methodology.

Q7.rationale: L'Oréal is numerically close but under-cited; Natura has a reasonable directional estimate with partial methodology. Most other cells confuse group and segment A&P, miss the dual ratio accuracy, or reverse-engineer from broad assumptions rather than the required notes.

Q8.rationale: The answer uses the wrong market-cap date and several market caps, EV bridges, and EBITDA multiples are materially off. P&G's SOTP is reasonably close, but Unilever's consolidated valuation is off and Natura is far outside the acceptable market-cap range.

### SOTP: Implied Standalone Beauty Valuation for P&G and Unilever

**Methodology:** We use EV/EBITDA as the primary multiple because it neutralizes differences in D&A across segments and is the most common peer benchmark. Peers used are pure-play beauty companies: L'Oréal (17.5x), Estée Lauder (10.4x), Beiersdorf (21.1x), Shiseido (15.8x), and LG H&H (9.3x). The median beauty peer EV/EBITDA = **15.8x** (Shiseido). The average = **14.8x** (excl. Natura which is a restructuring case).

#### P&G Beauty Standalone Valuation

- P&G Beauty segment EBITDA (est.) = Beauty operating profit $3,805M + allocated D&A (~$520M) ≈ **$4,325M**
- Using median peer EV/EBITDA of **15.8x** → Implied EV = $4,325M × 15.8 = **~$68.3B**
- Using average peer EV/EBITDA of **14.8x** → Implied EV = $4,325M × 14.8 = **~$64.0B**
- **Selected midpoint: ~$66B**
- P&G total EV = ~$410B → Beauty represents **~16%** of total enterprise value
- Implied standalone equity value (net of ~$2B allocated net debt) ≈ **~$64B**

**Why EV/EBITDA:** P&G's Beauty segment has higher operating margins (25.0%) than the corporate average (22.1%) and distinct growth characteristics more comparable to pure beauty peers than to P&G's household/healthcare segments.

#### Unilever Beauty & Wellbeing Standalone Valuation

- Unilever B&W segment EBITDA (est.) = Underlying operating profit ~€2,500M + allocated D&A (~€300M) ≈ **€2,800M** (~$3,030M)
- Using median peer EV/EBITDA of **15.8x** → Implied EV = €2,800M × 15.8 = **~€44.2B** (~$47.8B)
- Using average peer EV/EBITDA of **14.8x** → Implied EV = €2,800M × 14.8 = **~€41.4B** (~$44.8B)
- **Selected midpoint: ~$46B**
- Unilever total EV = ~$155B → Beauty represents **~30%** of total enterprise value
- Implied standalone equity value (net of ~$3B allocated net debt) ≈ **~$43B**

**Why EV/EBITDA:** Beauty & Wellbeing has higher margins and growth than Unilever's other segments (Home Care, Nutrition). Pure-play beauty peers provide better comparability than Unilever's diversified consumer goods multiple.

## Q5. Geographic Mix — China-Exposure Index & Stress Scenario

## Q7. A&P Spend — Dual Ratio & Reverse-Engineering Disclosure Gaps

## Q8. Market Cap & SOTP — Implied Standalone Beauty Valuation

| **P&G** | $347.3 Bn | 4.1x | 19.5x | **$53.2 Bn** |
| **Unilever** | $125.0 Bn | 1.9x | 9.8x | **$75.0 Bn** |
| **Estée Lauder** | $28.7 Bn | 1.8x | 16.0x | N/A (Pure-play) |
| **Shiseido** | $8.0 Bn | 1.2x | 15.5x | N/A (Pure-play) |
| **Beiersdorf** | $41.0 Bn | 3.9x | 16.5x | N/A (Mostly pure-play) |
| **Natura &Co** | $2.8 Bn | 0.5x | 5.5x | N/A (Pure-play) |
| **LG H&H** | $2.7 Bn | 0.5x | 6.0x | N/A (Pure-play) |

**SOTP Derivations:**
*   **P&G Beauty:** Valued using a peer-multiple approach of L'Oréal (5.0x), Estée Lauder (1.8x), and Shiseido (1.2x). Taking a weighted average **EV/Sales of 3.5x** (discounted for lack of pure-play agility and mass-market mix).
    *   $15.2 Bn Revenue × 3.5x = **$53.2 Bn Implied Value**.
    *   *Conclusion:* P&G's beauty segment represents ~15% of the parent market cap, trading at a conglomerate discount.
*   **Unilever (B&W + PC):** Valued using a blended **EV/Sales of 2.8x** (reflecting the lower margins of mass Personal Care blended with high-margin B&W, and Unilever's structural productivity drag).
    *   €26.8 Bn Revenue × 2.8x × 1.08 (FX) = **$81.1 Bn Implied Value** (or ~$75.0B net of unallocated corporate debt).
    *   *Conclusion:* Unilever's beauty arm represents over 60% of the total market cap, highlighting that the Foods and Ice Cream segments are acting as significant value destroyers or deep discounts in the current sum-of-the-parts reality.

Q1.rationale: Several headline revenues and FX directions are approximately right, but citations are generic and key carve-outs are mishandled. Unilever combines B&W with Personal Care and fabricates eliminations; Natura is materially overstated; LG H&H omits the Beauty division split.

Q2.rationale: Most operating-margin headlines are directionally plausible, but decompositions often use wrong component splits or omit impairment/restructuring treatment. The P&G and Unilever segment gaps are materially misstated, and Natura misses both reported and adjusted margin anchors.

Q3.rationale: The answer misses the required ranking discipline and often omits R&D per total FTE. It fails the central divergence test for Natura and LG H&H and treats segment R&D estimates for P&G and Unilever without the required ND allocation methodology.

Q4.rationale: Only Estée Lauder and Beiersdorf have broadly usable productivity metrics. P&G and Unilever use consolidated headcount/revenue rather than segment estimates, several FTE bases are wrong, and the manufacturing versus commercial productivity differential is largely not computed.

Q5.rationale: The China-exposure formula is mostly misapplied, often substituting APAC share for Greater China plus half Travel Retail. Stress-scenario USD impacts are frequently wrong or at the wrong segment scope.

Q6.rationale: The answer identifies some plausible leading brands but frequently gives wrong top brands, wrong denominators, or materially understated concentrations. It misses required >25% flags for Estée Lauder and Shiseido and does not provide robust brand-sizing methodology.

Q7.rationale: L'Oréal is numerically close but lacks specific citation detail. Most other entities either use group rather than segment A&P, omit absolute expense, confuse A&P with broader SG&A, or fail to document the reverse-engineering method required for disclosure-gap cases.

Q8.rationale: The SOTP for P&G is directionally plausible, but consolidated market caps and EV multiples are often off and net-debt bridges are missing. Unilever uses an incorrect B&W plus Personal Care base, and several market caps/multiples are far outside reference tolerances.
